gbm_population_evidence.quote: Recurrent Malignant Glioma; Recurrent WHO Grade 3 Glioma; Recurrent WHO Grade 4 Glioma; WHO Grade 2 Glioma; WHO Grade 3 Glioma; WHO Grade 4 Glioma
Diagnosis or clinical suspicion of recurrent malignant glioma, including:

candidate_evidence.quote: Anti-GARP Chimeric Antigen Receptor-T Cells (other names: Anti-GARP CAR T Cells (SY), Anti-GARP CAR T-cells (SY), Anti-GARP CAR-T Cells (SY)): Given intracavitary

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Anti-GARP Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cell Therapy for the Treatment of Recurrent Grade III or IV Gliomas

role_evidence.quote: CAR T-cell therapy is a type of treatment in which a patient's T cells (a type of immune system cell) are changed in the laboratory so they will attack tumor cells.

agents.drug_class_hint: autologous CAR-T cell therapy targeting GARP (cell therapy, excluded type)

source_quote.quote: Correlation of GARP expression levels with outcomes: Relative GARP expression in tumor tissue will be summarized using descriptive statistics.

coder_notes: Population: grade 2-4 recurrent glioma; glioblastoma is not named, but 'WHO Grade 4 Glioma' without an IDH requirement appears in conditions, which under D27C counts as historical glioblastoma, hence mixed_glioma_gbm_named / historical. If D27C were read as not applying to mixed grade 2-4 glioma conditions, this would be high_grade_glioma_unspecified; screening outcome is unaffected because the only agent is a CAR-T cell therapy (excluded type). GARP is the CAR-T target, not matched because there is no pharmacological candidate.
